input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: When ANSI is stripped, the code also calls `.strip()` on the whole prompt text. That removes the prompt's meaningful leading and trailing whitespace, including the usual trailing space (e.g. `"Name: "` becomes `"Name:"`).
- rationale: Trigger: a prompt such as `"Name: "` or `"Continue? [y/N]: "` shown on a non-tty stream or when color is disabled. `strip_ansi(text).strip()` drops the trailing space, so the user's input is typed directly against the colon. Leading indentation is lost too. Output differs depending on whether ANSI stripping is active, and `strip_ansi` alone would have been enough.
critique: The finding names the same mechanism as the label: after strip_ansi, the code calls .strip(), which removes the trailing space of a prompt like 'Name: ' when color is not supported. The consequences also line up: input ends up glued to the colon, and output differs between color and non-color environments.
